results.corrected_extracted: The Hunter Area Toxicology Service is a regional toxicology unit; every overdose presentation and admission is entered prospectively into a clinical database by two trained staff who were blind to the hypotheses. Of 9960 admissions between 13 January 1987 and 22 November 2002, 2222 involved at least one serotonergic drug taken in overdose; this test dataset had no exclusions and includes the derivation dataset. Derivation dataset: 473 admissions with a single SSRI, after excluding 9 with two SSRIs and any with a tricyclic antidepressant, MAOI, venlafaxine, nefazodone, lithium or an anti-serotonergic drug taken as well. Of the 473, 73 (15.4%, 95%CI 12.3–19.0) had a diagnosis of serotonin toxicity made by a clinical toxicologist, 70 (14.8%, 95%CI 11.7–18.4) met Sternbach's criteria and 44 (9.3%, 95%CI 6.8–12.3) were treated with a 5-HT2A antagonist. The tree analysis was done in the SSRI-alone dataset; the rules were tested on the complete dataset. The paper reports no age values, sex, breakdown by drug or amounts (age was tested, p = 0.004, with no direction given).
